title: Policy sidecar: semantic route-contract resolver and runtime validator
creator: Maya Chen
description: Introduce a lightweight policy-sidecar service that performs semantic validation and runtime resolution of routing contracts (region selection, tier routing, fallback model variants) before rules are accepted into the distributed routing plane. This ticket captures design + implementation for the sidecar validator, type-checked rule AST, and an in-memory contract resolver that prevents unsafe fallbacks and guarantees deterministic fallback ordering.
background: Current routing DSL validation is split between compile-time linters and downstream runtime heuristics. We've observed subtle failures during rollouts where incompatible fallback variants or region constraints result in silent degraded behavior. A sidecar that runs transactional semantic checks and exposes a deterministic resolution result will let us safely accept complex rules and enable fast rollouts across Dedicated and Private deployments.
details: Sidecar will run as an opt-in admission step in the control plane: when a policy change is submitted, the sidecar validates and returns a canonical resolution (JSON contract) that the router can apply atomically.

Validation steps: schema validation -> typed AST generation -> semantic checks (region/tier intersection, capacity-awareness heuristics) -> fallback loop detection -> cost/latency tier compatibility checks.
Canonical resolution includes: selected region candidates (ordered), preferred tiers, model variant chain (primary -> fallbacks), and safety metadata (reason codes, suggested mitigations).

The sidecar will maintain a small set of environment-specific heuristics (capacity classes per region, model runtime compatibility matrix) stored as versioned data used during validation. Heuristics must be editable via a config API and versioned with the release tag.
API surface: /validate -> returns pass/fail + canonical contract; /explain -> human-readable reasoning for UI and audit logs; /simulate -> best-effort runtime simulation given mock capacity.
We will integrate with Console to show explainable failures and suggested fixes (links to docs/PRs).
acceptance_criteria: Sidecar binary built and deployed to staging that accepts DSL input and returns a canonical contract for 95% of existing policy patterns.
Unit tests cover typed AST generation and fallback loop detection with >= 90% branch coverage for the validator module.
Integration tests that simulate region outage and verify that resolver produces safe fallback chains with explicit safety metadata.
Console shows validator errors and suggested fixes for 5 common misconfigurations.
Benchmarks: median validation latency < 120ms for typical policy size (< 30 rules) and peak < 500ms for large policy bundles.
Security review completed and sidecar config API requires RBAC to edit heuristics.
Docs: PRD and design doc linked, migration guide for existing rules included.
Canary rollout plan exists and is approved by SRE and Product.
Corresponding e2e test added to routing-integration suite.
Release notes drafted for runtime-1.20 describing semantic validation behavior and potential breaking changes.
implementation_notes: Phase 1 (spike): prototype typed AST and fallback loop detection as a library module in Go (2 week spike).
Phase 2: package as sidecar gRPC/HTTP service, add explain endpoint, and wire to control-plane admission (3 sprints).
Phase 3: integration with Console explain UI, add simulation endpoint, and create migration tool to backfill canonical contracts (1 sprint).
Use protobuf for the canonical contract schema to guarantee stable wire format across components.
Schema must be backward compatible; include version field and a compatibility test harness.
Plan to reuse existing kernel of region/tier heuristics from routing runtime but separate read-only copy for the sidecar to avoid lock contention.
Fallback detection algorithm: build directed graph of variant transitions and run cycle detection; annotate nodes with reason codes (cap, latencyMismatch, modelIncompatible).
Expose metrics: validation.success, validation.latency_ms (p50/p95), validation.fail_reason_count{reason}, contract.size_bytes.
Add feature flag to allow staged enforcement: allow failures to be warnings for first 2 weeks per org before blocking.
Add e2e regression tests that assert deterministic contract ordering for identical input on multiple runs.
Implementation language: Go for sidecar to align with control plane and runtime libs; library components designed so they can be compiled into other languages if needed.
Storage: heuristics/compat matrix stored in a small versioned YAML in S3/Blobstore; sidecar fetches on startup and polls for changes.
Operational runbook for troubleshooting validation failures and rollback path for sidecar config changes.
Docs/PRs: design doc at https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Policy+Sidecar+Design and initial spike PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/routing-lib/pull/1420.

risks: Validators introducing new blocking behavior could cause customer-facing rule rejections during rollout. Mitigation: warnings-first flag and staged enforcement.
Maintaining heuristic parity with runtime may drift; need automated compatibility checks and daily canary validations.
Validation latency may increase control plane write latency; mitigate via caching canonical contracts and async validation for very large bundles.
Edge cases where runtime has implicit fallbacks not encoded in DSL; we must expand DSL or add adapters to capture those cases.
Operational complexity: new service to run and maintain (monitoring/runbook required).
Security: heuristics editing surface must be RBAC-protected to avoid malicious policy acceptance.
Backward compatibility: older routers must ignore unknown fields; ensure protobuf + compatibility tests.
Potential for increased QA workload to cover combinatorial policy permutations; use property-based tests to reduce gaps.
High-risk dependency: requires completed work in ENG-61437 to stabilize runtime compatibility matrix.
Data: must ensure no sensitive customer data is logged by explain endpoint; scrub inputs.
Model variant naming mismatch between model catalog and routing DSL may cause false incompatibilities; add a normalization layer.
Performance: validation p95 > 500ms could block control-plane writes under load; include circuit-breaker and fallback to permissive mode.
Rollback plan: feature flag disables sidecar enforcement and backfills previous contracts in control-plane cache.
Estimate uncertainty: spike might reveal more complex compatibility rules requiring extra sprints.
Monitoring: false positives in explain UI could increase support load; provide clear remediation steps and links to PRDs.
Documentation debt: insufficient examples for common tenant configurations will cause repeated support requests.
Any change touching admission flow must be coordinated with Sales and Customer Success for large customers expecting SLA stability.
